run.question: List the top 5 largest Elasticsearch indices matching the pattern 'app-184-*' by document count. Show their names and doc counts.

report.summary: The request was an inventory lookup, not an incident investigation. A docs.count-descending listing of indices matching 'app-184-*' returned 1800 indices; the first five rows (all with 500 documents) are the five largest, and a follow-up count confirms exactly 5 of the 1800 indices hold 500 documents, so the top five is unambiguous rather than an arbitrary tie-break. All five are green and open. The ranking reflects index state at query time only, not the incident window.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch listing of pattern 'app-184-*' sorted by docs.count descending (columns index,health,status,docs.count,store.size) matched 1800 indices; the returned slice's first five rows all show docs.count "500": app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25 (green, open, 45.7kb), app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10 (green, open, 44.7kb), app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20 (green, open, 45.8kb), app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05 (green, open, 46.8kb) and app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15 (green, open, 29.9kb).

A jq aggregation over all indices matching 'app-184-*' (columns index,docs.count) returned total=1800, top_docs=500 and at_500=5, i.e. only five indices in the pattern carry the maximum document count of 500, so no index outside the five listed exceeds them.

All five largest indices report health "green" and status "open" in the same listing, with store sizes between 29.9kb (app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15) and 46.8kb (app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05).

gaps: Index listings carry no time range: the document counts are the state at the moment of the query (observed_at 2026-11-21T08:39:43Z), so they do not establish index sizes during the authorized incident window 2026-11-20T08:39:40Z to 2026-11-21T08:39:40Z.

The first full listing exceeded the view limit (RESULT_TOO_LARGE, 1800 rows); rows 5-1799 were not read individually, so per-index health/size for indices outside the top five is unknown (their doc counts are bounded below 500 by the jq aggregation).
Only the first 5 rows of the descending sort were inspected; the ordering among the 1795 lower-ranked indices was not examined.
next_steps: If sizes at a specific past time are needed, query the indices with an explicit time-bounded aggregation rather than the current listing.

view.cannot_prove: This is the state at the moment of the query only: it cannot prove which indices, fields or document counts existed during the incident window, nor that any document lies in that window. A field that is mapped is not proof that documents carry it.
